2026-09-01.title: Start the Month with God
2026-09-01.verse: Psalm 90:12 - So teach us to number our days that we may get a heart of wisdom.
2026-09-01.text: September begins with a fresh page, but a new month only becomes meaningful when we place it in God's hands. Psalm 90:12 reminds us that our days are limited and therefore valuable. A wise man does not simply fill his calendar; he learns to invest his time in what matters eternally. Work, responsibilities, goals, and family demands can quickly consume our attention, but none of them should push God to the margins. Before you make plans for this month, ask the Lord to shape your priorities. What needs to change? What deserves more attention? What distraction needs to lose its place? Begin September with prayer, Scripture, and a deliberate decision to walk closely with God. A month surrendered to Him can become more fruitful than a year directed only by your own strength.

2026-09-02.title: Strength for Today's Responsibilities
2026-09-02.verse: Isaiah 40:31 - But they who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles.
2026-09-02.text: Many men carry invisible weight: work deadlines, financial concerns, family responsibilities, ministry commitments, and personal battles no one else sees. Isaiah 40:31 does not promise a life without pressure; it promises renewed strength for those who wait on the Lord. Waiting on God is not passive resignation. It is choosing to trust His timing, seek His presence, and receive strength before trying to solve everything alone. You do not have to prove your manhood by carrying every burden silently. Bring your weakness to God. Ask for wisdom before reacting, patience before speaking, and endurance before giving up. The Lord can give you strength that does not come from adrenaline or determination. Today, do what is yours to do, but refuse to carry what belongs in God's hands.

2026-09-03.title: Integrity When No One Is Watching
2026-09-03.verse: Proverbs 11:3 - The integrity of the upright guides them, but the crookedness of the treacherous destroys them.
2026-09-03.text: Character is revealed most clearly when there is no audience. Proverbs 11:3 teaches that integrity is not merely a reputation; it is an internal compass that guides a man's decisions. It shows up in the websites you visit, the numbers you report, the promises you keep, the conversations you have, and the thoughts you choose to entertain. Small compromises rarely remain small. They slowly train the heart to tolerate what once troubled the conscience. God calls you to something better: a life that is the same in private and in public. Ask yourself where you are most tempted to make excuses. Bring that area honestly before God and choose obedience before the pressure comes. Integrity may cost convenience, money, or approval, but it gives something far more valuable: a clear conscience and a life that can stand securely before God.

2026-09-04.title: Be Present at Home
2026-09-04.verse: Deuteronomy 6:6-7 - And these words that I command you today shall be on your heart. You shall teach them diligently to your children.
2026-09-04.text: A man can provide financially for his family and still be emotionally absent from it. Deuteronomy 6 places spiritual formation inside ordinary daily life: sitting at home, walking along the way, lying down, and rising up. That means your family needs more than occasional advice; they need your presence. They need to see how you respond to stress, how you apologize, how you pray, how you treat others, and how you make decisions. If you have children, they are learning from your example even when you are not intentionally teaching. If you are a husband, your attention communicates value to your wife. Put the phone down for a while. Ask a meaningful question. Pray with your family. Listen without rushing to fix everything. The strongest spiritual influence you may have today could happen around your own table.

2026-09-05.title: Purpose Beyond Success
2026-09-05.verse: Mark 8:36 - For what does it profit a man to gain the whole world and forfeit his soul?
2026-09-05.text: Success can be a good servant but a dangerous master. Jesus asks a question in Mark 8:36 that exposes the emptiness of achievement without spiritual direction. A man may build a career, earn recognition, accumulate possessions, and still lose sight of the condition of his soul. God is not against excellence, ambition, or progress; He is against allowing temporary accomplishments to replace eternal priorities. Take inventory today. Is your definition of success shaped more by culture than by Christ? Are you becoming the kind of man your achievements are supposed to represent? Let your goals remain under God's authority. Work hard, learn, build, and provide, but do not sacrifice your character, family, health, or faith on the altar of advancement. The greatest success is to finish your race having been faithful to what God actually asked of you.

2026-09-06.title: Rest Is Not Weakness
2026-09-06.verse: Mark 6:31 - Come away by yourselves to a desolate place and rest a while.
2026-09-06.text: Jesus told His disciples to rest. That alone should challenge the idea that exhaustion is proof of faithfulness. Many men treat constant activity as a badge of honor, yet a tired mind makes poorer decisions, a tired heart becomes impatient, and a tired spirit can lose sensitivity to God's voice. Biblical rest is not laziness. It is recognition that you are a creature, not the Creator. You have limits, and accepting them is an act of humility. Create space today to slow down before God. Step away from noise for a while. Sleep if you need sleep. Take a walk. Pray without rushing. Let your mind settle. Your value does not increase because you are always busy. God can accomplish His purposes without your constant motion. Rest received with gratitude can prepare you to return to your responsibilities with greater clarity, patience, and strength.

2026-09-07.title: Courage to Do What Is Right
2026-09-07.verse: Joshua 1:9 - Be strong and courageous. Do not be frightened, and do not be dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
2026-09-07.text: Courage is not the absence of fear; it is obedience in the presence of fear. Joshua faced responsibilities far larger than himself, yet God's command was not to feel fearless. It was to move forward because God's presence was greater than the uncertainty ahead. You may be facing a difficult conversation, a career decision, a family crisis, a spiritual responsibility, or a change you did not choose. Fear often exaggerates what could go wrong and minimizes what God can do. Do not let anxiety make your decisions for you. Pray, seek wise counsel, examine Scripture, and then take the next faithful step. You do not need to see the entire road before moving. God's promise to Joshua still reveals an enduring truth: the man who walks in God's will never walks alone. Courage grows when your confidence shifts from yourself to the God who goes with you.

2026-09-08.title: Control Your Words
2026-09-08.verse: Proverbs 18:21 - Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruits.
2026-09-08.text: Words can strengthen a home or poison it. They can restore confidence or leave wounds that last for years. Proverbs 18:21 reminds us that speech carries real power. As men, we may excuse harshness as honesty, sarcasm as humor, or silence as self-control, but God cares about both truth and the spirit in which truth is spoken. Before speaking today, ask whether your words are necessary, accurate, and gracious. Especially when you are angry, slow down. A sentence spoken in ten seconds can create damage that requires months to repair. Use your voice to bless your wife, encourage your children, honor your coworkers, defend someone who is absent, and speak truth without cruelty. A strong man is not one who dominates a room with his voice; he is one whose words can be trusted because they are governed by wisdom and love.

2026-09-09.title: Lead by Serving
2026-09-09.verse: Mark 10:45 - For even the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.
2026-09-09.text: Jesus completely redefined leadership. In the world, leadership often means position, recognition, and control. In the kingdom of God, leadership begins with service. Christ had all authority, yet He used His strength for the good of others. That is the model for every Christian man who leads at home, at work, in church, or in the community. Ask yourself whether the people around you experience your leadership as a blessing or merely as pressure. Do you listen? Do you help with tasks that seem beneath your role? Do you give credit? Do you protect the dignity of others? Servant leadership does not mean weakness or lack of direction. It means using authority without selfishness. Today, look for one practical way to make someone else's burden lighter. Leadership that looks like Jesus may not always receive applause, but it leaves people stronger than it found them.

2026-09-10.title: Guard Your Mind
2026-09-10.verse: Philippians 4:8 - Whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is commendable... think about these things.
2026-09-10.text: Your mind is constantly being discipled by something. News, social media, entertainment, conversations, memories, fears, and desires all compete for attention. Philippians 4:8 gives a deliberate filter for what deserves repeated mental space. This does not mean ignoring problems or pretending life is easy. It means refusing to allow darkness, lust, resentment, or anxiety to become the default atmosphere of your thoughts. Pay attention to what you repeatedly consume and what it produces in you. Does it make you more peaceful, more faithful, more disciplined, and more compassionate? Or more angry, distracted, envious, and restless? You cannot control every thought that appears, but you can decide which thoughts you feed. Replace destructive patterns with Scripture, prayer, gratitude, wholesome conversation, and purposeful work. A guarded mind becomes fertile ground for wise decisions and a steady life.

2026-09-11.title: Faithful in Small Things
2026-09-11.verse: Luke 16:10 - One who is faithful in a very little is also faithful in much.
2026-09-11.text: We often imagine that character will reveal itself when a great opportunity arrives, but Jesus points us toward the small things. Faithfulness is built in ordinary decisions: arriving when you said you would, paying what you owe, finishing what you started, caring for details, keeping private information private, and doing good work even when no one notices. Men sometimes pray for greater influence while neglecting the responsibilities already in their hands. God often prepares us for more by watching how we handle less. Look around your life today. What small assignment have you been postponing? What promise needs to be kept? What routine needs more discipline? Do not despise ordinary obedience. A faithful life is usually constructed quietly, one decision at a time. When the bigger moment comes, you will not suddenly become dependable; you will reveal the dependability you have been practicing all along.

2026-09-12.title: Peace Under Pressure
2026-09-12.verse: John 14:27 - Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you.
2026-09-12.text: Pressure can expose what rules the heart. When plans fail, money is tight, people disappoint us, or the future becomes uncertain, anxiety easily takes control. Jesus offers a different kind of peace, one that does not depend on circumstances becoming easy. His peace comes from knowing that we belong to Him and that our lives remain under His care. This does not remove responsibility. You may still need to make a phone call, solve a problem, apologize, work harder, or seek help. But you can do those things without surrendering your inner life to panic. When you feel tension rising today, stop and breathe a simple prayer: 'Jesus, rule my heart with Your peace.' Then focus on the next faithful action rather than every possible outcome. Peace is not denial; it is confidence that God remains present even before the problem is resolved.

2026-09-13.title: A Man Who Forgives
2026-09-13.verse: Colossians 3:13 - As the Lord has forgiven you, so you also must forgive.
2026-09-13.text: Forgiveness is one of the strongest things a man can practice because it requires surrendering the desire to make another person pay emotionally forever. Colossians 3:13 grounds our forgiveness in what Christ has already done for us. Forgiving does not mean calling evil good, erasing consequences, or returning immediately to unsafe trust. It means releasing personal vengeance and refusing to let the offense control your heart. Some wounds require time, wise boundaries, and serious conversations, but bitterness should not become your permanent companion. Ask God to show you where resentment has been living too long. Name the hurt honestly before Him. Then begin releasing the person into God's justice and mercy. You may need to repeat that choice many times. A forgiving man is not a man without scars; he is a man who refuses to let his scars define the direction of his life.

2026-09-14.title: Honor Your Marriage
2026-09-14.verse: Ephesians 5:25 - Husbands, love your wives, as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her.
2026-09-14.text: Biblical love is far deeper than attraction or emotion. Ephesians 5:25 gives husbands a demanding model: Christ's self-giving love for the church. That means marriage is not primarily about asking whether your wife is meeting all your expectations; it is also about asking how faithfully you are reflecting Christ in the relationship. Love listens. Love protects. Love tells the truth with kindness. Love serves when tired. Love remains loyal when feelings fluctuate. If you are married, consider what your wife needs from you today—not in theory, but specifically. Maybe she needs your attention, an apology, practical help, encouragement, affection, or prayer. Do not wait for a special occasion to invest in your marriage. Strong marriages are built through thousands of ordinary acts of faithfulness. Let your home see a form of masculinity shaped not by selfish control, but by sacrificial love.

2026-09-15.title: Work as Worship
2026-09-15.verse: Colossians 3:23 - Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men.
2026-09-15.text: Work can easily become either an idol or a burden. Scripture offers a better perspective: work can become an act of worship when it is done for the Lord. Colossians 3:23 applies whether your task feels important or unnoticed. Excellence is not about impressing people; it is about honoring God with the abilities and opportunities He has given you. That changes the way you answer emails, serve customers, manage employees, study, drive, repair, build, teach, or clean. It also protects you from living only for applause. People may overlook your effort, but God sees faithfulness. At the same time, working for God does not mean becoming addicted to productivity. It means bringing integrity, diligence, and gratitude into your responsibilities while remembering that your identity is still in Christ. Do today's work well, and let the quality of your effort become a quiet testimony.

2026-09-16.title: Choose Discipline Over Mood
2026-09-16.verse: 1 Corinthians 9:27 - But I discipline my body and keep it under control.
2026-09-16.text: Feelings are real, but they make poor masters. Paul describes a life of intentional discipline because spiritual maturity does not happen automatically. There will be mornings when you do not feel like praying, days when exercise seems inconvenient, moments when anger feels justified, and seasons when responsibility feels exhausting. Discipline helps you act according to conviction rather than mood. Start with one area where inconsistency is costing you something. Do not attempt a dramatic transformation overnight. Establish a small practice you can repeat: ten focused minutes in Scripture, a daily walk, a defined bedtime, a spending limit, or a pause before responding in anger. Discipline is not punishment; it is training. Each time you say no to an impulse in order to say yes to a higher purpose, you strengthen your capacity to live intentionally. A disciplined man is freer because he is less controlled by appetite and circumstance.

2026-09-17.title: Ask for Wisdom
2026-09-17.verse: James 1:5 - If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach.
2026-09-17.text: Men are often expected to have answers, but Scripture gives us permission to admit when we do not know what to do. James 1:5 turns uncertainty into an invitation to pray. Wisdom is more than intelligence or experience; it is the ability to see a situation from God's perspective and respond in a way that honors Him. Before making an important decision, resist the impulse to move merely because you feel pressure to act. Gather facts. Seek counsel from mature believers. Examine your motives. Consider who will be affected. Most importantly, ask God for wisdom with an open heart, willing to obey the answer even if it challenges your preference. Sometimes wisdom leads forward; sometimes it says wait; sometimes it tells you to walk away. You do not become weaker by asking for guidance. You become safer, humbler, and more prepared to lead well.

2026-09-18.title: Do Not Fight Every Battle
2026-09-18.verse: Proverbs 19:11 - Good sense makes one slow to anger, and it is his glory to overlook an offense.
2026-09-18.text: Not every offense deserves a confrontation. Some issues require truth, boundaries, and courageous conversation, but others simply reveal our ego. Proverbs 19:11 connects wisdom with being slow to anger and willing to overlook an offense. A mature man learns the difference between a real problem and a wounded pride. Before reacting today, ask: Will addressing this bring healing, clarity, or justice? Or am I simply trying to prove that I am right? Social media, workplace tension, family misunderstandings, and everyday inconveniences constantly offer invitations to unnecessary conflict. You do not have to accept every invitation. Sometimes strength looks like silence. Sometimes it looks like a calm conversation later. Sometimes it looks like choosing mercy and moving on. Save your energy for battles that actually matter. Peace is not cowardice when it comes from wisdom and self-control.

2026-09-19.title: Brotherhood Matters
2026-09-19.verse: Ecclesiastes 4:9-10 - Two are better than one... For if they fall, one will lift up his fellow.
2026-09-19.text: Isolation can feel easier because it avoids vulnerability, but it also removes one of God's important protections for a man's life. Ecclesiastes reminds us that when one falls, another can help him rise. Every man needs trustworthy people who can encourage him, challenge him, pray with him, and ask questions deeper than 'How are you?' Strong friendships do not happen automatically in adulthood; they require intention. Reach out to a brother in faith. Share something real. Ask how he is doing spiritually, not just professionally. If you are struggling, resist the instinct to disappear until you have fixed yourself. God often uses other people as part of His answer. Likewise, be the kind of friend who notices when someone else is becoming quiet or withdrawn. Brotherhood is not merely companionship. At its best, it becomes a place where men help one another remain faithful.

2026-09-20.title: Teach by Example
2026-09-20.verse: Titus 2:7 - Show yourself in all respects to be a model of good works, and in your teaching show integrity, dignity.
2026-09-20.text: The most convincing lesson you will ever teach is the life you live repeatedly. Titus calls believers to become models of good works because example gives credibility to instruction. This is especially important for fathers, mentors, leaders, and older men. People quickly notice the gap between what we say and what we practice. If you tell others to pray but never pray, speak about honesty while cutting corners, or demand respect while treating people poorly, your message loses power. You do not need to be perfect to be an example. In fact, humility in failure can teach just as much as success. Admit when you are wrong. Ask forgiveness. Keep learning. Let younger men see what repentance, responsibility, and perseverance look like in real life. Your influence grows when people can safely imitate not only your words, but also the direction of your life.

2026-09-21.title: Trust God with Provision
2026-09-21.verse: Matthew 6:31-33 - Do not be anxious, saying, 'What shall we eat?' or 'What shall we drink?' ... But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness.
2026-09-21.text: Financial pressure can reach deep into a man's sense of responsibility. Providing matters, and Scripture commends diligence, planning, and wise stewardship. But Jesus warns against allowing provision to become anxiety's doorway into the heart. Matthew 6 does not encourage irresponsibility; it reorders priorities. Seek God's kingdom first, then handle your responsibilities from a place of trust rather than panic. Review your finances honestly. Cut what needs to be cut. Work faithfully. Ask for counsel if necessary. Avoid comparing your life with people whose circumstances you do not fully know. Most importantly, remember that your worth as a man is not equal to your income. Seasons change. Jobs change. Economies change. God remains faithful. Do what wisdom requires today and refuse to let fear write tomorrow's story before it arrives.

2026-09-22.title: Return Quickly When You Fail
2026-09-22.verse: 1 John 1:9 - If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
2026-09-22.text: Failure becomes most dangerous when shame convinces us to hide from God. First John 1:9 gives the opposite invitation: confess and return. A mature Christian man is not someone who never sins; he is someone who learns to repent quickly and honestly. Stop defending what God is asking you to surrender. Name the sin without minimizing it. Accept responsibility for any damage you caused. Make restitution where appropriate. Then receive the forgiveness Christ offers instead of punishing yourself endlessly. Grace does not make sin unimportant; it makes restoration possible. The enemy wants failure to become your identity. The gospel says failure can become the place where humility and dependence grow. If you fell yesterday, you do not need to remain there today. Get up, return to God, and take the next obedient step. His mercy is greater than your worst moment.

2026-09-23.title: Be Slow to Anger
2026-09-23.verse: James 1:19-20 - Let every person be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger; for the anger of man does not produce the righteousness of God.
2026-09-23.text: Anger can make a man feel powerful while quietly taking away his control. James gives a three-part pattern that can transform conflict: listen quickly, speak slowly, and delay anger. Most arguments escalate because we reverse that order. We react quickly, listen poorly, and then defend the damage. Being slow to anger does not mean never addressing wrongdoing. Jesus confronted injustice, but He was never controlled by uncontrolled rage. When tension rises today, create space between the feeling and the response. Lower your voice. Ask a question. Take a short break if necessary. Pray before sending the message. Try to understand what the other person is actually saying. Self-control is not weakness; it is strength under authority. The goal is not merely to win an argument, but to respond in a way that allows God's righteousness rather than your wounded pride to shape the outcome.

2026-09-24.title: Make Room for God's Word
2026-09-24.verse: Psalm 119:105 - Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
2026-09-24.text: We often ask God for direction while giving little attention to the primary source of truth He has already provided. Psalm 119 describes Scripture as a lamp—not a floodlight that reveals every detail of the future, but enough light for the next step. The Bible shapes judgment, exposes motives, corrects assumptions, and reminds us who God is when emotions become unreliable. You do not need an elaborate study plan to begin. Read a manageable passage slowly. Ask what it reveals about God, what it exposes in you, and what obedience would look like today. Write down one sentence if that helps you remember. Consistency matters more than volume. Over time, Scripture builds a framework for decisions long before the crisis arrives. A man whose mind is regularly formed by God's Word is less likely to be ruled by trends, pressure, fear, or impulse.

2026-09-25.title: Use Your Influence Well
2026-09-25.verse: Matthew 5:16 - Let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven.
2026-09-25.text: You influence more people than you realize. Your coworkers notice how you handle pressure. Your family notices what receives your attention. Younger men observe what you normalize. Even your online behavior says something about what you value. Jesus calls His followers to let their light shine, not so they can become impressive, but so that God receives glory. Influence is stewardship. Ask yourself what your life is teaching without words. Are people seeing patience, integrity, generosity, courage, and hope? Or are they mainly seeing frustration, ego, and self-promotion? You do not need a platform to have influence. Faithfulness in ordinary relationships can shape generations. Use your voice to encourage rather than humiliate. Use your position to protect rather than control. Use your experience to guide rather than boast. Let people leave your presence with a clearer picture of the character of Christ.

2026-09-26.title: Contentment in a Comparing World
2026-09-26.verse: Philippians 4:11 - I have learned in whatever situation I am to be content.
2026-09-26.text: Comparison has become easier than ever. In minutes, you can see another man's income, body, family, vacation, ministry, house, or achievements and begin to feel behind. Paul says contentment is something he learned. That means it is a spiritual skill developed through practice, not a personality trait some people simply possess. Contentment does not eliminate ambition or healthy goals. It frees you from needing someone else's life in order to appreciate your own. Thank God for what is already in your hands. Celebrate another man's success without treating it as evidence of your failure. Evaluate your goals according to your calling, not someone else's highlight reel. There may be things you genuinely need to improve, but improvement driven by gratitude is healthier than progress driven by envy. Contentment allows you to work hard without despising the season God has given you today.

2026-09-27.title: Protect What Enters Your Heart
2026-09-27.verse: Proverbs 4:23 - Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life.
2026-09-27.text: Proverbs tells us to guard the heart because everything else flows from it. What you repeatedly allow inside eventually shapes your desires, reactions, and decisions. This is especially important in a world designed to capture attention. Not every movie, account, conversation, joke, or private habit deserves access to your inner life. Guarding your heart does not mean living in fear of culture. It means developing discernment about what strengthens holiness and what slowly weakens it. Pay attention to patterns. What makes temptation stronger? What fuels resentment? What leaves you spiritually numb? Remove unnecessary access before temptation becomes a crisis. Replace unhealthy inputs with better ones: Scripture, meaningful friendships, constructive learning, service, exercise, and time with your family. Boundaries are not evidence that you are weak. Wise boundaries are one of the ways strong men remain strong.

2026-09-28.title: Carry Someone Else's Burden
2026-09-28.verse: Galatians 6:2 - Bear one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
2026-09-28.text: Strength was never meant to be used only for yourself. Galatians 6:2 calls believers to help carry the weight others cannot easily carry alone. Sometimes that means practical help. Sometimes it means listening. Sometimes it means giving money, making a phone call, visiting someone, praying consistently, or simply showing up. Men can be uncomfortable around another person's pain because we want to fix what may not have an immediate solution. But presence itself can be ministry. Ask God to make you attentive today. Who around you seems unusually tired, quiet, discouraged, or overwhelmed? Instead of saying only, 'Let me know if you need anything,' offer something concrete. Carrying another person's burden will cost time and convenience, but it reflects the heart of Christ, who carried a burden for us that we could never carry ourselves.

2026-09-29.title: Finish What You Started
2026-09-29.verse: 2 Timothy 4:7 - I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
2026-09-29.text: Starting is exciting; finishing requires character. Paul looked back near the end of his life and could say he had finished the race and kept the faith. Many good intentions remain unfinished because motivation fades when the work becomes repetitive. Look at the commitments God has already placed before you. Is there a responsibility you keep postponing, a project you abandoned too quickly, a conversation you promised to have, or a spiritual habit you repeatedly restart? Not everything should be finished—sometimes wisdom requires changing direction—but do not quit simply because the novelty is gone. Break the remaining work into a manageable next step and do that step today. Faithfulness is often less dramatic than we imagine. It is continuing when no one is cheering. Build the kind of life that can someday look back with gratitude and say, by God's grace, 'I stayed faithful to the end.'

2026-09-30.title: End the Month with Gratitude
2026-09-30.verse: Psalm 103:2 - Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits.
2026-09-30.text: At the end of a month, it is easy to focus only on what remains unfinished. Psalm 103 invites us to remember God's benefits. Before rushing into October, look back. Where did God provide? What prayer was answered? What lesson did you learn? Where were you protected from something you did not even recognize at the time? What relationship grew? What failure taught you humility? Gratitude does not require pretending that September was easy. Some prayers may still be unanswered and some burdens may still be present. But remembering God's faithfulness keeps unfinished problems from becoming the only story you tell yourself. Write down three specific things for which you are grateful. Thank God for them by name. Then place the next month in His hands. The man who remembers God's past faithfulness enters the future with stronger confidence in God's continued care.
